title: Double mask-Dice emphasis using standard Transformers configuration

single_material_change.effect: Doubles mask Dice in both Hungarian assignment cost and weighted supervised loss (main/aux/encoder); source loss_rf_detr.py uses this parameter in both locations. It is not an assignment-frozen loss-only ablation.

hypothesis: Stronger per-instance mask overlap emphasis improves small roof segmentation and neighbour separation enough to increase matched small-roof recall at fixed .5. DEV association motivates this test but does not prove the mechanism; object-score filtering may instead dominate.
baseline: Frozen epoch4/.5 DEV plus already-completed unchanged-recipe epochs5-7; no new baseline run
starting_point: B3 epoch4 with its optimizer/scheduler/RNG; new run ID and new candidate identity, never overwrite a checkpoint
unchanged: Karnataka TRAIN3581 chips, including880 empties and all zero-pixel features
RGB432 source profile, tile512 stride384, flips, seed26011
batch1 accumulation4, BF16, headLR1e-4 backboneLR1e-5, clip.1
DEV1434 chips and threshold.5 for stopping and primary comparison

cost_estimate.basis: B4 three epochs plus three-threshold DEV scoring took47min; same shapes, no extra tensor allocation expected. Estimate, not a measured fit.

stop_condition: Maximum3 additional epochs or70min at a checkpoint boundary
Three epochs without recall improvement over epoch4 at.5
Immediate stop before update on nonfinite loss/gradients or >6GiB reserved
No unchanged retries after failed bounded result

success_criteria.selection: DEV only at fixed.5; targets must be met together, not threshold-picked after failure

evaluation: DEV-only comparison with matched feature attribution and size/adjacency bins. No independent accuracy or transfer claim. A later production-quality claim needs lead-approved genuinely fresh preregistered region before candidate selection, evaluated once; do not reuse Coxs Bazar or Karnataka HOLDOUT.
approval_needed: Lead authorizes the new objective experiment and GPU ownership window.
